recipes.title: Scottish Porridge With Blueberries And Flaxseeds
recipes.description: Oats contain beta-glucan, a soluble fibre shown in randomised trials to reduce LDL cholesterol and moderate post-prandial glucose — particularly important during hormonal therapy f…
recipes.clinical_notes: Oats contain beta-glucan, a soluble fibre shown in randomised trials to reduce LDL cholesterol and moderate post-prandial glucose — particularly important during hormonal therapy for breast cancer where insulin resistance is elevated. Blueberries supply pterostilbene and anthocyanins that inhibit oestrogen-receptor-alpha signalling in vitro (University of Liverpool, 2021). Flaxseeds are the richest plant source of lignans (secoisolariciresinol diglucoside), which are converted by gut bacteria to enterolactone — a compound shown in the UK Million Women Study to be associated with reduced breast cancer recurrence. WCRF UK recommends wholegrains at every meal for cancer survivors.
ingredients: 250ml semi-skimmed milk or fortified oat milk
instructions: Place oats and milk in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Stir continuously for 5–7 minutes until porridge reaches desired consistency.
Remove from heat. Stir in ground flaxseeds.
Transfer to bowl. Top with blueberries, walnuts, and cinnamon.
Drizzle with honey or maple syrup if desired. Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Wholemeal Seeded Toast With Avocado And Poached Egg
recipes.description: Avocado provides oleic acid (the predominant fatty acid in olive oil) which has been shown to suppress HER2 overexpression in breast cancer cell lines (Selvaraj et al., 2019).
recipes.clinical_notes: Avocado provides oleic acid (the predominant fatty acid in olive oil) which has been shown to suppress HER2 overexpression in breast cancer cell lines (Selvaraj et al., 2019). Poached eggs supply all essential amino acids for muscle protein synthesis — crucial as cancer cachexia affects 20–40% of breast cancer patients on chemotherapy. Wholemeal bread's insoluble fibre accelerates bowel transit, reducing contact time between potential carcinogens and the colonic mucosa. The Royal Marsden's dietetic guidelines recommend eggs as a primary protein source for patients with reduced appetite.
instructions: Toast bread until golden.
Halve and stone avocado. Scoop flesh into bowl, mash with lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Bring a small pan of water to a gentle simmer. Add a splash of white vinegar.
Crack each egg into a small cup. Create a gentle whirlpool and slide egg in. Poach 3 minutes for runny yolk.
Spread avocado on toast. Top with poached egg. Season with salt, pepper, and chilli flakes if using.
Scatter fresh herbs and serve immediately.

recipes.title: Berry And Greek Yoghurt Parfait With Walnuts
recipes.description: Greek yoghurt contains live Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium cultures that restore gut microbiome diversity disrupted by chemotherapy-induced dysbiosis.
recipes.clinical_notes: Greek yoghurt contains live Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium cultures that restore gut microbiome diversity disrupted by chemotherapy-induced dysbiosis. Walnuts are uniquely rich in alpha-linolenic acid (ALA) and ellagic acid; a 2021 UCLA clinical study found walnut consumption altered gene expression in breast tumours towards less aggressive phenotypes. Add half the berries, then a spoonful of granola.
Repeat with remaining yoghurt, berries, and granola.
Scatter chopped walnuts on top. Drizzle with honey.
Serve immediately or refrigerate up to 2 hours.

recipes.title: Smoked Salmon And Scrambled Eggs On Rye
recipes.description: Smoked salmon provides 2.2g of EPA+DHA omega-3 fatty acids per 100g serving — the highest dietary source of these anti-inflammatory lipids.
recipes.clinical_notes: Smoked salmon provides 2.2g of EPA+DHA omega-3 fatty acids per 100g serving — the highest dietary source of these anti-inflammatory lipids. Multiple meta-analyses confirm marine omega-3s reduce pro-inflammatory eicosanoids (PGE2, LTB4) that promote breast tumour angiogenesis. Omega-3s also ameliorate chemotherapy-induced cognitive impairment ('chemo brain'). Rye bread has a lower glycaemic index (55) than wheat bread, supporting insulin sensitivity during hormonal therapies. WCRF UK specifically recommends oily fish twice weekly for cancer survivors.

instructions: Toast rye bread until warm but not hard.
Whisk eggs with milk and black pepper.
Melt butter in non-stick pan over low heat. Add egg mixture.
Stir slowly with silicone spatula, folding gently, removing from heat when just set and creamy.
Arrange smoked salmon on rye toast. Top with scrambled eggs.
Garnish with fresh dill, capers, and a squeeze of lemon.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Seed And Chia Power Granola
recipes.description: Pumpkin seeds are one of the richest plant sources of zinc (10mg/100g), a mineral essential for T-cell function and wound healing — particularly important post-mastectomy or radiot…
recipes.clinical_notes: Pumpkin seeds are one of the richest plant sources of zinc (10mg/100g), a mineral essential for T-cell function and wound healing — particularly important post-mastectomy or radiotherapy. Their phytosterols have been shown to inhibit 5-alpha reductase and modulate hormone-sensitive pathways. Chia seeds provide complete omega-3 ALA profile and form a gel in the gut that slows glucose absorption, supporting blood sugar stability during steroid-based anti-emetic regimens. This granola can be prepared in large batches (stores 3 weeks) — practical for low-energy treatment days.
instructions: Preheat oven to 170°C (fan 150°C).
Mix oats, pumpkin seeds, sunflower seeds, chia seeds, and nuts in large bowl.
Combine melted coconut oil, maple syrup, vanilla, cinnamon, and salt. Pour over dry mixture and stir well.
Spread on lined baking tray in an even layer.
Bake 20 minutes, stir once halfway, until golden.
Remove and cool completely — it crisps as it cools.
Stir in dried cranberries. Store in airtight jar.
Serve with yoghurt or plant milk.

instructions: Heat olive oil in a wide, deep frying pan over medium heat.

Add garlic and peppers, cook 5 minutes.
Add spices, stir 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in tinned tomatoes. Season generously. Simmer 10 minutes until sauce thickens.
Make 4 wells in sauce. Crack one egg into each well.
Cover pan and cook 5–7 minutes until whites are set but yolks still soft.
Scatter parsley and crumbled feta if using. Serve with warm pitta.

recipes.title: Warm Apple And Cinnamon Buckwheat Porridge
recipes.description: Buckwheat — despite its name — is a gluten-free pseudo-grain rich in rutin, a flavonoid that strengthens capillary walls and reduces treatment-related bruising and bleeding.
recipes.clinical_notes: Buckwheat — despite its name — is a gluten-free pseudo-grain rich in rutin, a flavonoid that strengthens capillary walls and reduces treatment-related bruising and bleeding. Its D-chiro-inositol improves insulin sensitivity, addressing the metabolic dysregulation common with corticosteroid use during chemotherapy. Apples provide quercetin and ursolic acid — compounds shown in UK laboratory studies to inhibit aromatase and reduce oestrogen synthesis in breast tissue. This warming preparation is particularly suitable during winter months and periods of chemotherapy-related cold sensitivity.
ingredients: 1 large Bramley or Granny Smith apple, peeled and diced
instructions: Toast rinsed buckwheat in a dry pan 3 minutes until nutty.
Add water and bring to boil. Reduce heat, simmer 15 minutes until groats are tender.
Meanwhile, cook diced apple in a small pan with 1 tbsp water and cinnamon for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir almond milk, vanilla, and maple syrup into buckwheat. Cook 2 more minutes.
Transfer to bowl. Top with cinnamon apple and flaked almonds.
Sprinkle extra cinnamon on top.

recipes.title: Turmeric And Ginger Golden Milk Porridge
recipes.description: Curcumin in turmeric has been investigated in over 30 UK clinical trials for its NF- κ B inhibitory properties.
recipes.clinical_notes: Curcumin in turmeric has been investigated in over 30 UK clinical trials for its NF- κ B inhibitory properties. When combined with black pepper's piperine, curcumin bioavailability increases 2000-fold. The combination has shown synergistic effects with docetaxel in phase II trials (Bayet-Robert et al., 2010). This anti-inflammatory combination is particularly beneficial during radiotherapy when localised inflammation peaks. Golden milk preparations are now included in the Maggie's Centre nutritional guidelines for breast cancer patients.
ingredients: 1/2 tsp ground ginger (or 1 tsp fresh grated ginger)
Pinch of black pepper (essential for curcumin absorption)
instructions: Combine oats, coconut milk, turmeric, ginger, cinnamon, and black pepper in a saucepan.
Bring to gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring frequently.
Cook 5–7 minutes until porridge thickens.
Sweeten with maple syrup.
Serve topped with desiccated coconut and banana slices.

recipes.title: High-Energy Seed And Nut Butter Toast
recipes.description: Patients with Stage III–IV breast cancer or those undergoing intensive chemotherapy regimens require calorie-dense foods to prevent cancer cachexia — a syndrome affecting 50% of ad…
recipes.clinical_notes: Patients with Stage III–IV breast cancer or those undergoing intensive chemotherapy regimens require calorie-dense foods to prevent cancer cachexia — a syndrome affecting 50% of advanced breast cancer patients and independently predicting poorer survival. Nut butters provide 590 kcal per 100g with beneficial monounsaturated fatty acids. Hemp seeds contain all 20 amino acids including all 9 essential amino acids in a 3:1 omega-6:omega-3 ratio that is optimal for reducing systemic inflammation. The Royal Marsden's nutritional support team recommends targeted calorie supplementation for patients with >5% unintentional weight loss.
ingredients: 2 thick slices wholegrain bread (sourdough or seeded loaf)
instructions: Toast bread to desired level.
Spread generously with nut butter — do not be sparse.
Arrange banana slices on top.
Scatter hemp seeds, pumpkin seeds, and granola if using.
Drizzle with honey and dust with cinnamon.
For extra calories: add a second layer of nut butter beneath the banana.

recipes.title: Bircher Muesli With Apple And Dried Apricots
recipes.description: This Swiss-origin preparation pre-soaks oats to break down phytic acid and increase iron and zinc absorption by up to 50% — critical during chemotherapy-induced mineral depletion.
recipes.clinical_notes: This Swiss-origin preparation pre-soaks oats to break down phytic acid and increase iron and zinc absorption by up to 50% — critical during chemotherapy-induced mineral depletion. Dried apricots provide beta-carotene (provitamin A) that is converted to retinol for immune modulation and skin integrity during radiotherapy. Apple pectin acts as a prebiotic for Lactobacillus species, restoring gut microbiome balance post-antibiotic use (common with neutropenic fever treatment). Can be prepared in 5-portion batches — essential for fatigue management.
ingredients: 2 apples (one grated into muesli, one sliced to serve)
instructions: Combine oats, apple juice, yoghurt, seeds, dried apricots, and grated apple in a large bowl.
Stir in lemon juice and honey.
Cover and refrigerate overnight (minimum 4 hours).
In the morning, stir and add a little more milk if too thick.
Divide into portions. Top with sliced apple and flaked almonds.
Will keep refrigerated for 3 days.

recipes.title: Cottage Cheese And Berry Protein Bowl
recipes.description: Cottage cheese provides 11g protein per 100g serving, making it one of the most protein-dense whole foods.
recipes.clinical_notes: Cottage cheese provides 11g protein per 100g serving, making it one of the most protein-dense whole foods. Its casein protein provides sustained amino acid release over 7 hours — superior to whey for overnight muscle protein synthesis, particularly important on rest days between chemotherapy cycles. The moderate leucine content (1.7g per 200g serving) just meets the threshold to maximally stimulate muscle protein synthesis. Low fat content makes it easily tolerated during periods of nausea. Conjugated linoleic acid (CLA) in dairy has independent anti-proliferative activity against breast cancer cell lines.
instructions: Spoon cottage cheese into a bowl.
Top with mixed berries, pumpkin seeds, and walnuts.
Drizzle with honey. Dust with cinnamon.
Stir ground flaxseeds through if using.
Eat immediately or chill for up to 4 hours.

recipes.title: Soft Boiled Eggs With Asparagus Soldiers
recipes.description: Asparagus is one of the richest food sources of folate (149μ g per 100g) and asparagine (its namesake amino acid), which is a precursor to aspartate — a neurotransmitter supporting…
recipes.clinical_notes: Asparagus is one of the richest food sources of folate (149μ g per 100g) and asparagine (its namesake amino acid), which is a precursor to aspartate — a neurotransmitter supporting cognitive function during chemotherapy. The rutin content of asparagus strengthens blood vessel walls, reducing the bruising and bleeding complications seen with anticoagulant therapy in breast cancer. Eggs supply selenium (15μ g per egg) — a cofactor for glutathione peroxidase, the body's primary antioxidant defence enzyme. The UK Biobank cohort study associated higher egg consumption with improved survival outcomes in breast cancer patients.
ingredients: 200g fresh asparagus spears, woody ends removed
instructions: Bring a small pan of water to a boil. Carefully lower in eggs. Cook 6 minutes for runny yolk.
Meanwhile, heat a griddle pan over high heat. Toss asparagus in olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Grill asparagus 4–5 minutes, turning occasionally, until tender and lightly charred.
Transfer eggs to egg cups. Tap and remove top of shell.
Serve with asparagus spears as dippers. Add wholemeal bread soldiers if desired.

recipes.title: High-Protein Vegan Tofu Scramble
recipes.description: Firm tofu provides complete protein (8g per 100g) with all essential amino acids.
recipes.clinical_notes: Firm tofu provides complete protein (8g per 100g) with all essential amino acids. Unlike animal protein, soy protein does not increase IGF-1 levels — a growth factor associated with breast cancer progression in observational studies. Turmeric added to this scramble creates the visual appearance of eggs while providing curcumin. Nutritional yeast provides vitamin B12 (often deficient in plant-based diets) and beta-glucans that enhance natural killer cell activity. Kale and peppers supply vitamins C, K, and beta-carotene supporting immune surveillance during and after treatment.
instructions: Press tofu firmly to remove excess water. Crumble into a bowl with your hands.
Heat oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat.
Fry garlic and spring onion 2 minutes.
Add crumbled tofu. Sprinkle turmeric and paprika over. Stir well to coat.
Cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly golden.
Add diced pepper and kale. Cook 3 more minutes.
Stir in nutritional yeast. Season generously.
Serve with cherry tomatoes and wholemeal toast.

recipes.title: Spinach And Mushroom Omelette
recipes.description: Eggs contain phosphatidylcholine (the primary dietary source), a precursor to acetylcholine — the neurotransmitter impaired in chemotherapy-induced cognitive dysfunction.
recipes.clinical_notes: Eggs contain phosphatidylcholine (the primary dietary source), a precursor to acetylcholine — the neurotransmitter impaired in chemotherapy-induced cognitive dysfunction. The choline content (294mg per 2 eggs) supports hepatic methylation essential for tamoxifen clearance. Mushrooms, particularly shiitake and chestnut varieties, contain beta-1,3/1,6-glucan polysaccharides (lentinan and PSK) that have been used as immunoadjuvants in Japanese oncology protocols. UK clinical trials are currently investigating mushroom polysaccharides as immunotherapy combination agents. Spinach provides thioredoxin reductase activation supporting tumour suppressor protein activity.
instructions: Whisk eggs with milk, salt, pepper, and fresh thyme.
Heat oil in an omelette pan over medium-high heat. Fry onion 3 minutes.
Add mushrooms. Cook 4 minutes until golden and any moisture has evaporated.
Add spinach and stir until wilted, about 2 minutes.
Push vegetables to one side. Pour egg mixture into pan.
As edges set, draw cooked egg towards centre with a spatula.
When almost set, scatter cheese over half the omelette. Fold in half over vegetables.
Slide onto plate and serve immediately.

recipes.clinical_notes: A traditional UK-South Asian fusion drink, the mango lassi adapted with turmeric and black pepper provides both probiotic bacteria (from yoghurt) and anti-inflammatory curcumin in a single serving. Blend on high until smooth and creamy.
Taste and adjust sweetness with more honey if desired.
Pour into a large glass over extra ice.
Drink immediately or keep refrigerated up to 24 hours.
Can be made in batches and frozen in portions.

recipes.title: Almond And Date Energy Balls
recipes.description: These no-cook energy balls provide 85 kcal each — a calorie-dense, bite-sized option for patients with reduced appetite or mouth sores who can only manage small portions.
recipes.clinical_notes: These no-cook energy balls provide 85 kcal each — a calorie-dense, bite-sized option for patients with reduced appetite or mouth sores who can only manage small portions. Medjool dates provide glucose and fructose for immediate energy, plus iron (1.7mg per 2 dates) supporting red blood cell production during chemotherapy-induced anaemia. Almonds provide vitamin E (alpha-tocopherol, 9mg per 30g), the fat-soluble antioxidant that protects cell membranes from oxidative damage during radiotherapy. These store for 3 weeks refrigerated — making them ideal for batch preparation before treatment cycles.
instructions: Place pitted dates in food processor. Pulse until they form a paste.
Add ground almonds, almond butter, cocoa powder, vanilla, and salt. Pulse until combined.
Roll tablespoon-sized portions into balls between your palms.
Roll each ball in desiccated coconut.
Place on a tray lined with baking paper. Refrigerate 30 minutes to firm up.
Store in airtight container in fridge for up to 3 weeks. Makes approximately 20 balls.

recipes.title: Courgette And Feta Breakfast Muffins
recipes.description: These savoury muffins can be prepared in batches of 12 and frozen, providing convenient high-nutrition meals for treatment days when cooking is impossible.
recipes.clinical_notes: These savoury muffins can be prepared in batches of 12 and frozen, providing convenient high-nutrition meals for treatment days when cooking is impossible. Courgette provides significant amounts of vitamin C (17mg per 100g) and potassium, supporting immune function and fluid balance during corticosteroid therapy. Feta cheese provides calcium (493mg/100g) essential for bone density maintenance during aromatase inhibitor treatment — an under-recognised concern for the 50,000+ UK women annually started on AIs. The egg and feta protein combination supports wound healing post-surgical procedures.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (fan 160°C).
Grate courgette, squeeze in a clean tea towel to remove maximum moisture.
Whisk eggs, oil, and milk together.
Combine flour, courgette, feta, cheddar, and seasoning in a bowl.
Pour egg mixture into dry ingredients. Fold together gently until just combined.
Spoon into muffin tin. Bake 22–25 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool 10 minutes before removing. Store in fridge 4 days or freeze 3 months.

Fresh strawberries and natural yoghurt to serve

Beat in eggs until combined.
Stir in ground flaxseeds, flour, baking powder, cinnamon, and maple syrup.
Let batter rest 5 minutes (flaxseeds thicken the batter).
Heat a small knob of coconut oil in a non-stick pan.
Drop tablespoons of batter into pan. Cook 2 minutes each side until golden.
Serve with fresh strawberries, yoghurt, and a drizzle of maple syrup.

recipes.title: Kale And Red Pepper Frittata
recipes.description: Red peppers contain 190mg of vitamin C per 100g — more than three times that of oranges.
recipes.clinical_notes: Red peppers contain 190mg of vitamin C per 100g — more than three times that of oranges. Vitamin C is a direct anti-tumour agent at pharmacological doses (IV vitamin C trials) and at dietary doses improves the absorption of non-haem iron from plant sources — reducing treatment-related iron-deficiency anaemia. Kale's glucosinolates (glucoraphanin, indole-3-carbinol) undergo hydrolysis to isothiocyanates and DIM that modulate oestrogen metabolism. The frittata format provides protein in a firm, easy-to-slice form appropriate for patients who cannot manage liquid foods but need consistent protein intake.
instructions: Preheat grill to high.
Heat oil in oven-proof frying pan over medium heat.
Fry onion 5 minutes until soft. Add garlic and red pepper, cook 4 minutes.
Add kale, cook 2 minutes until wilted. Season well.
Beat eggs with salt, pepper, and half the cheese.
Pour egg mixture over vegetables in the pan. Cook on hob 3–4 minutes until edges set.
Scatter remaining cheese over the top.
Transfer to grill. Cook 4–5 minutes until top is golden and frittata is set through.
Cool 5 minutes before slicing into wedges.

recipes.title: Brown Rice Congee With Ginger And Spring Onion
recipes.description: Rice congee (jook) is a traditional healing preparation particularly recommended for patients with severe mucositis (Grade 3–4 oral sores) or significant neutropenia where most foo…
recipes.clinical_notes: Rice congee (jook) is a traditional healing preparation particularly recommended for patients with severe mucositis (Grade 3–4 oral sores) or significant neutropenia where most foods cannot be safely or comfortably consumed. The prolonged cooking of brown rice creates a near-liquid starchy porridge that coats the oesophageal mucosa, providing soothing relief. Ginger has the strongest clinical evidence of any dietary intervention for chemotherapy-induced nausea (ASCO guidelines, 2020). Spring onion provides quercetin and thiosulfinates with antimicrobial activity — important during immunosuppression. This recipe is safe for neutropenic diets (all ingredients thoroughly cooked).
ingredients: 2cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and grated
1 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce or tamari
instructions: Rinse rice thoroughly.
Add rice and stock to a large pot. Bring to boil, then reduce to lowest simmer.
Cook uncovered for 60–90 minutes, stirring occasionally, until rice breaks down and congee is creamy.
Add grated ginger, soy sauce, and sesame oil.
Ladle into bowls. Top with spring onion.
If serving to neutropenic patients, ensure all ingredients are well cooked; use only the cooked portion of spring onion.

recipes.title: Almond Flour Blueberry Muffins
recipes.description: For the estimated 15–20% of breast cancer patients with concurrent coeliac disease or non-coeliac gluten sensitivity, almond flour provides a gluten-free alternative that is also h…
recipes.clinical_notes: For the estimated 15–20% of breast cancer patients with concurrent coeliac disease or non-coeliac gluten sensitivity, almond flour provides a gluten-free alternative that is also higher in protein and healthy fats than wheat flour. Blueberries contain the highest antioxidant capacity of all commonly consumed UK fruits (ORAC score 4,669), providing pterostilbene that crosses the blood-brain barrier to reduce chemotherapy-associated cognitive impairment. instructions: Preheat oven to 170°C. Line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases.
Whisk together eggs, maple syrup, melted coconut oil, and vanilla.
Stir in almond flour, baking powder, salt, and lemon zest.
Gently fold in blueberries.
Divide batter between cases (each about 2/3 full).
Bake 20–22 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in tin 10 minutes, then transfer to wire rack.
Store in airtight container for 4 days or freeze for 2 months.

Pour liquid mixture over dry ingredients. Mix thoroughly.
Press firmly into lined tin — compress well with the back of a spoon.
Bake 25 minutes until golden.
Cool completely in tin before cutting into 12 bars.
Wrap individually and store in fridge for 2 weeks or freeze for 3 months.

recipes.description: Chia seeds swell to form a pudding texture requiring no cooking — one of the only preparations naturally suitable for patients with severe xerostomia (dry mouth) caused by salivary…
recipes.clinical_notes: Chia seeds swell to form a pudding texture requiring no cooking — one of the only preparations naturally suitable for patients with severe xerostomia (dry mouth) caused by salivary gland irradiation. Cover and refrigerate overnight (minimum 4 hours).
Blend thawed raspberries to a smooth coulis. Sweeten with a little extra maple syrup if desired.
Remove chia pudding from fridge. Stir well — it should be thick and creamy.
Spoon into glasses. Pour raspberry coulis over.
Top with fresh raspberries and flaked coconut.

recipes.title: Baked Beans On Wholemeal Toast
recipes.description: The humble baked bean is nutritionally underrated: a tin of baked beans provides 20g fibre, 20g plant protein, and significant lycopene from tomato sauce.

instructions: Heat baked beans in a small saucepan over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until hot.
Toast wholemeal bread until golden.
Rub cut side of garlic clove over toasted bread.
Drizzle bread lightly with olive oil.
Spoon beans over toast. Season with black pepper.
Optional: scatter grated cheese and fresh parsley over.
Serve immediately — comfort food at its most nutritionally honest.

Bake 40–45 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool 15 minutes in tin before turning out. Slice when completely cool.
Store wrapped for 4 days or freeze sliced for 2 months.

recipes.title: Soft Stewed Prunes With Greek Yoghurt

recipes.clinical_notes: Opioid analgesics used in Stage III–IV breast cancer pain management cause constipation in over 60% of patients — a significant quality-of-life concern. Prunes (dried plums) contain sorbitol (a natural laxative, 14.7g/100g) and dihydroxyphenyl isatin, which directly stimulates intestinal contractions. A 2011 Iowa State University RCT found 100g prunes daily was more effective than psyllium husk for constipation relief. Greek yoghurt provides Lactobacillus acidophilus and Bifidobacterium lactis that reduce opioid-induced gut dysbiosis. This gentle breakfast is recommended in Macmillan's bowel management guidelines for cancer patients.
instructions: Place prunes, water, vanilla extract, and cinnamon stick in a small saucepan.
Bring to simmer. Cook 10–15 minutes until prunes are very soft and sauce has thickened.
Remove cinnamon stick. Cool slightly.
Spoon Greek yoghurt into a bowl. Arrange warm stewed prunes alongside.
Drizzle honey over yoghurt. Scatter flaked almonds if using.
Eat while prunes are still warm — this aids digestion.

recipes.title: Peach And Chamomile Smoothie
recipes.description: Cancer diagnosis and treatment are associated with clinically significant anxiety in 40–60% of patients.
recipes.clinical_notes: Cancer diagnosis and treatment are associated with clinically significant anxiety in 40–60% of patients. Chamomile contains apigenin — a flavonoid that binds GABA-A receptors with mild anxiolytic activity. A 2009 University of Pennsylvania RCT found chamomile extract significantly reduced generalised anxiety disorder symptoms. Peaches provide beta-cryptoxanthin, a carotenoid specifically associated with reduced breast cancer risk in the EPIC cohort study (Castelló et al., 2017). The soothing liquid format makes this an appropriate morning preparation for patients with treatment-related morning anxiety or nausea.
ingredients: 100g natural yoghurt or silken tofu (for vegan)
instructions: Brew chamomile tea with 2 tea bags in 300ml boiling water. Steep 10 minutes. Cool completely.
Add cooled tea, frozen peach slices, yoghurt or tofu, honey, vanilla, and flaxseeds to blender.
Blend until smooth. Add ice cubes and blend again.
Pour into glass. Drink slowly for best effect.

recipes.title: Quinoa And Pomegranate Breakfast Bowl
recipes.description: Quinoa provides all 9 essential amino acids in a single grain — exceptionally rare in the plant kingdom.
recipes.clinical_notes: Quinoa provides all 9 essential amino acids in a single grain — exceptionally rare in the plant kingdom. Its ecdysterone content has been shown to reduce IGF-1 receptor signalling in cell culture models. Pomegranate seeds contain punicalagins — the most potent dietary antioxidants known (3x the antioxidant capacity of red wine and green tea). A 2013 City of Hope Medical Center study found pomegranate extract inhibited aromatase enzyme activity in breast tissue — providing a food-based adjunct to aromatase inhibitor therapy. This preparation provides visual appetite appeal through colour diversity — important when treatment reduces appetite.
instructions: Place cooled cooked quinoa in a bowl.
Whisk together tahini, lemon juice, honey, and 1 tbsp water to make a dressing.
Drizzle tahini dressing over quinoa. Mix gently.
Arrange pomegranate seeds, orange segments, and pistachios over quinoa.
Garnish with fresh mint leaves.
Serve at room temperature — allows maximum phytonutrient expression.

recipes.title: Warm Lemon Ginger Water With Honey
recipes.description: This simple morning drink should precede any breakfast — particularly during chemotherapy cycles.
recipes.clinical_notes: This simple morning drink should precede any breakfast — particularly during chemotherapy cycles. Warm water with fresh ginger stimulates gastric secretions and intestinal motility. Lemon juice stimulates bile production from the liver, supporting fat-soluble vitamin absorption and hepatic detoxification pathways used to metabolise chemotherapy drugs. Honey provides antimicrobial methylglyoxal (particularly in Manuka honey) that reduces oral mucositis bacterial colonisation. Macmillan Cancer Support recommends staying well hydrated (2 litres/day) to reduce chemotherapy side effects and support kidney clearance of toxic metabolites. This preparation counts towards daily fluid targets.
ingredients: 2cm piece fresh ginger, grated or thinly sliced
instructions: Heat water to approximately 60°C — warm but comfortable to drink.
Add lemon juice, grated ginger, and honey.
Stir until honey dissolves.
Add a pinch of turmeric for extra anti-inflammatory benefit.
Sip slowly before breakfast.
Can be made in a flask and sipped throughout the morning.

recipes.title: Savoury Lentil Pancakes
recipes.description: Red lentils are among the highest-folate foods available (179μ g per 100g cooked) — essential for women on methotrexate therapy and for all patients where DNA repair mechanisms mus…
recipes.clinical_notes: Red lentils are among the highest-folate foods available (179μ g per 100g cooked) — essential for women on methotrexate therapy and for all patients where DNA repair mechanisms must be supported. Lentil protein (25g per 100g dry) provides arginine, an amino acid that is required for T-lymphocyte function and wound healing. These naturally gluten-free pancakes are suitable for the cohort of breast cancer patients with concurrent coeliac disease. The iron in red lentils (3.3mg/100g) is enhanced by the lemon juice commonly served alongside — addressing chemotherapy-induced anaemia.
ingredients: 150g red lentils, soaked 30 minutes and drained
Tomato and cucumber salsa to serve
instructions: Blend soaked, drained lentils with water until smooth batter forms.
Stir in cumin, turmeric, coriander, chilli, and salt.
Heat oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Pour small ladleful of batter per pancake. Spread gently.
Cook 3 minutes until edges are dry, flip, cook 2 more minutes.
Serve warm with tomato salsa and a dollop of natural yoghurt.

recipes.title: Classic British Lentil And Vegetable Soup
recipes.description: Red lentils form the nutritional backbone of this British staple.
recipes.clinical_notes: Red lentils form the nutritional backbone of this British staple. Their isoflavone content (including daidzein at 9.4μ g/g) contributes to the phyto-oestrogen profile shown to reduce breast cancer recurrence in post-menopausal Asian populations. The soup's soluble fibre (predominantly from lentils and root vegetables) reduces enterohepatic oestrogen circulation by binding oestrogen glucuronides in the gut. WCRF UK Second Expert Report classifies dietary fibre as having 'strong evidence' for cancer risk reduction. This soup is suitable for all cancer stages and all side effect profiles — a true universal preparation.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Sauté onion and garlic 5 minutes until soft and golden.
Add cumin, turmeric, and paprika. Stir 1 minute.
Add carrots, celery, rinsed lentils, chopped tomatoes, and stock.
Bring to boil. Reduce heat and simmer 25–30 minutes until lentils are completely soft.
Season well. Partially blend for a smooth-chunky texture if desired.
Ladle into bowls. Garnish with fresh parsley.
Serve with thick slices of wholemeal bread.

recipes.title: Broccoli And Stilton Soup
recipes.description: Broccoli is the most researched brassica vegetable for cancer prevention.
recipes.clinical_notes: Broccoli is the most researched brassica vegetable for cancer prevention. Its sulforaphane (formed when glucoraphanin is activated by myrosinase) is a potent Nrf2 activator that upregulates Phase II detoxification enzymes and has direct anti-proliferative effects on breast cancer cells (Spencer et al., 2021, UK). Sulforaphane bioavailability is increased 3-fold by briefly chewing raw broccoli before cooking or adding raw broccoli powder to cooked soups. Stilton cheese provides calcium for bone protection during AI therapy and vitamin K2 for carboxylation of osteocalcin. UK dietitians recommend cruciferous vegetables three times weekly for breast cancer survivors.

recipes.title: Tomato, Red Pepper And Basil Soup
recipes.description: Lycopene — the carotenoid responsible for tomatoes' red colour — is the subject of over 35 clinical studies in breast cancer.
recipes.clinical_notes: Lycopene — the carotenoid responsible for tomatoes' red colour — is the subject of over 35 clinical studies in breast cancer. Lycopene inhibits IGF-1-stimulated breast cancer cell growth and has been shown to reduce circulating levels of IGF-1 in women at high breast cancer risk (UK Sherfield Study, 2018). Cooking with olive oil dramatically increases lycopene bioavailability compared to raw tomatoes. Red peppers add capsaicin in small amounts, which has been shown to trigger apoptosis in triple-negative breast cancer cells — the most clinically challenging subtype. The vibrant orange-red colour stimulates appetite in patients with treatment-related anorexia.

recipes.title: Roasted Butternut Squash And Ginger Soup
recipes.description: Butternut squash provides 4,293μ g of beta-carotene per 100g — converted to vitamin A for maintenance of mucosal integrity of the gut lining, which is commonly disrupted by chemoth…
recipes.clinical_notes: Butternut squash provides 4,293μ g of beta-carotene per 100g — converted to vitamin A for maintenance of mucosal integrity of the gut lining, which is commonly disrupted by chemotherapy. The immune-supportive role of vitamin A extends to NK cell activation and T-regulatory cell modulation. Fresh ginger (1–2cm added to this soup) provides the gingerols shown in systematic review to reduce acute chemotherapy-induced nausea with a clinical effect size comparable to metoclopramide (Pillai et al., 2011). This vibrant orange soup is one of the most frequently recommended preparations by Macmillan cancer nurses.

recipes.title: Cock-A-Leekie Soup (Chicken And Leek)
recipes.description: This Scottish national dish provides lean chicken protein (amino acid profile optimal for muscle synthesis) along with leeks — members of the allium family alongside garlic and oni…
recipes.clinical_notes: This Scottish national dish provides lean chicken protein (amino acid profile optimal for muscle synthesis) along with leeks — members of the allium family alongside garlic and onions. Leeks contain kaempferol and quercetin that have been shown in a 2019 UK study to reduce proliferation of ER-positive breast cancer cells by inhibiting cyclin-dependent kinases. The collagen-rich homemade bone broth base provides glycine and proline for gut lining repair after chemotherapy-induced enteritis. NHS Scotland cancer dietetics services recommend Cock-a-Leekie as a traditional, culturally familiar, high-protein soup for Scottish breast cancer patients.

recipes.clinical_notes: Watercress is the richest UK dietary source of phenethyl isothiocyanate (PEITC) — an isothiocyanate that has been shown in a University of Southampton clinical study (Lund et al., 2018) to reduce DNA damage markers in blood cells of smokers and has demonstrated anti-angiogenic properties in breast cancer models. This bright green soup derives appetite appeal from its intense colour and fresh flavour — qualities particularly valued when taste alterations (dysgeusia) from platinum chemotherapy reduce enjoyment of food.

recipes.description: Carrots and oranges together provide a synergistic combination of beta-carotene (in carrots) and vitamin C (in orange juice) that dramatically increases iron absorption from plant-…
recipes.clinical_notes: Carrots and oranges together provide a synergistic combination of beta-carotene (in carrots) and vitamin C (in orange juice) that dramatically increases iron absorption from plant-based meals. The alpha-carotene in carrots (distinct from beta-carotene) is specifically associated with reduced breast cancer mortality in a 2018 UK Biobank analysis. Fresh coriander provides flavonoids including quercetin and apigenin that have been shown to sensitise triple-negative breast cancer cells to doxorubicin chemotherapy. The bright orange colour provides visual pleasure and appetite stimulation for patients with treatment-induced anorexia.

recipes.title: Mulligatawny Soup (Vegetarian Uk Adaptation)
recipes.description: Mulligatawny — meaning 'pepper water' — is a colonial-era British-Indian soup that has become a UK national dish.
recipes.clinical_notes: Mulligatawny — meaning 'pepper water' — is a colonial-era British-Indian soup that has become a UK national dish. This adaptation uses red lentils and root vegetables, providing anti-inflammatory curry spices alongside dense plant protein. Curry spices (cumin, coriander, garam masala, turmeric) each have documented bioactive compounds relevant to breast cancer biology: cumin's thymoquinone inhibits VEGF-mediated angiogenesis; coriander's linalool has pro-apoptotic activity; garam masala's clove eugenol inhibits NF- κ B signalling. The rich spice profile stimulates appetite and overcomes the taste blunting (dysgeusia) common during platinum and taxane chemotherapy.

recipes.title: Tuscan White Bean And Kale Soup (Ribollita)
recipes.description: Ribollita derives from the Tuscan peasant tradition of re-boiling (ribollire) leftover minestrone.
recipes.clinical_notes: Ribollita derives from the Tuscan peasant tradition of re-boiling (ribollire) leftover minestrone. This re-cooking actually increases the bioavailability of lycopene and beta-carotene from tomatoes and kale through the break-down of cellular matrices. White beans (cannellini) provide resistant starch that is fermented by colonic bacteria to produce short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) including butyrate, propionate, and acetate — compounds that inhibit histone deacetylases and activate tumour suppressor genes. Kale adds sulforaphane precursors (glucoraphanin). The WCRF Second Expert Report identifies the Mediterranean dietary pattern (of which this soup is archetypal) as associated with a 12% reduction in breast cancer risk.

recipes.title: Creamy Cauliflower And Turmeric Soup
recipes.description: Cauliflower — a brassica vegetable — provides 3-methylsulfinylpropyl glucosinolate (glucoiberin) that is hydrolysed to iberin, an isothiocyanate with similar but distinct activity…
recipes.clinical_notes: Cauliflower — a brassica vegetable — provides 3-methylsulfinylpropyl glucosinolate (glucoiberin) that is hydrolysed to iberin, an isothiocyanate with similar but distinct activity to sulforaphane. Iberin has been shown to specifically target breast cancer stem cells — the population responsible for treatment resistance and metastatic relapse. Turmeric in this soup is best combined with black pepper and a small amount of fat (provided by coconut oil in this recipe) to maximise curcumin absorption. The mild, cream-like texture of puréed cauliflower makes this soup suitable even for Grade 3 mucositis when many other foods are intolerably painful.

recipes.title: Miso And Shiitake Mushroom Noodle Soup
recipes.description: Miso is a fermented soybean paste providing live Aspergillus oryzae cultures alongside substantial genistein content.
recipes.clinical_notes: Miso is a fermented soybean paste providing live Aspergillus oryzae cultures alongside substantial genistein content. The Hiroshima/Nagasaki study found that women who consumed miso soup twice daily had 54% lower breast cancer incidence despite living in a high-radiation environment — suggesting the fermented soy compounds provide both anti-oestrogenic and radioprotective effects. Shiitake mushrooms provide lentinan — a beta-glucan polysaccharide licensed as an intravenous immunomodulator in Japan for cancer patients. At dietary doses, lentinan from shiitake mushrooms activates dendritic cells and NK cells, supporting the immune surveillance that prevents recurrence.

recipes.title: Smoked Haddock Chowder (Uk Classic)
recipes.description: Smoked haddock provides 23g high-biological-value protein per 100g serving plus 175μ g iodine — essential for thyroid function that may be compromised by radiotherapy to the neck r…
recipes.clinical_notes: Smoked haddock provides 23g high-biological-value protein per 100g serving plus 175μ g iodine — essential for thyroid function that may be compromised by radiotherapy to the neck region. Iodine is also required for thyroid hormone production that regulates basal metabolic rate — critical for preventing the hypothyroidism-like fatigue symptoms some breast cancer patients experience. The chowder's dairy base provides calcium, phosphorus, and vitamin D (from milk). UK dietary guidance from the NHS specifically recommends oily and white fish as high-quality protein sources during cancer treatment.

recipes.title: Gazpacho (Cold Tomato Soup)
recipes.description: Gazpacho retains the full spectrum of heat-sensitive vitamins from raw tomatoes, peppers, and cucumber — including vitamin C (completely destroyed by cooking above 70°C), and the m…
recipes.clinical_notes: Gazpacho retains the full spectrum of heat-sensitive vitamins from raw tomatoes, peppers, and cucumber — including vitamin C (completely destroyed by cooking above 70°C), and the myrosinase enzyme from garlic that activates allicin. Raw garlic allicin has direct antimicrobial activity against Helicobacter pylori and has been shown in UK population studies to be associated with reduced gastric cancer risk. The cooling temperature of gazpacho provides symptomatic relief for oral mucositis and radiation-induced xerostomia. For patients on neutropenic diets, a briefly pasteurised version can be prepared by heating to 75°C and then rapidly cooling.

recipes.title: Jerusalem Artichoke And Hazelnut Soup
recipes.description: Jerusalem artichokes (not artichokes at all, but related to sunflowers) provide inulin — the most potent prebiotic dietary fibre known.
recipes.clinical_notes: Jerusalem artichokes (not artichokes at all, but related to sunflowers) provide inulin — the most potent prebiotic dietary fibre known. 100g provides 16–20g inulin that specifically stimulates Bifidobacterium and Lactobacillus species, the beneficial bacteria shown to enhance immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy responses in cancer patients (Zitvogel et al., 2018). The strong prebiotic effect is particularly valuable for restoring gut microbiome balance after antibiotic courses. Note: introduce gradually to minimise flatulence in sensitive patients. Hazelnuts add vitamin E and manganese — cofactors for antioxidant enzyme systems.

recipes.title: Spiced Beetroot And Apple Soup
recipes.description: Beetroot's vivid colour derives from betalains — a class of pigments (betacyanins and betaxanthins) distinct from all other food pigments that have demonstrated anti-proliferative…
recipes.clinical_notes: Beetroot's vivid colour derives from betalains — a class of pigments (betacyanins and betaxanthins) distinct from all other food pigments that have demonstrated anti-proliferative and pro-apoptotic effects on breast cancer cell lines in a 2020 UK study. Betanin specifically inhibits cyclin D1 expression, slowing breast cancer cell division. The high nitrate content of beetroot (250mg/100g) is converted to nitric oxide, improving tumour vascularity and potentially increasing chemotherapy drug delivery to poorly perfused tumour regions. Apple pectin adds prebiotic fibre, and the combination creates a soup with a visually striking deep purple-red colour that stimulates appetite.

recipes.title: Chickpea And Spinach Curry (Chana Palak)
recipes.description: Chickpeas provide a unique combination of isoflavones, saponins, and resistant starch that together address multiple breast cancer risk pathways.
recipes.clinical_notes: Chickpeas provide a unique combination of isoflavones, saponins, and resistant starch that together address multiple breast cancer risk pathways. Their phytosterols compete with cholesterol for intestinal absorption — reducing the cholesterol substrate available for synthesis of oestrone and oestradiol in peripheral tissues. Spinach's iron (2.7mg/100g non-haem) is substantially enhanced when paired with the vitamin C in tomatoes — achieving near-haem absorption efficiency. This combination is particularly important for patients with chemotherapy-induced anaemia who cannot tolerate iron supplements. The curry spice blend (cumin, coriander, garam masala) each contributes bioactive phytochemicals with documented breast cancer relevance.
ingredients: Fresh coriander and natural yoghurt to serve
instructions: Heat oil in a large deep pan over medium heat.
Fry onion 8 minutes until deeply golden — do not rush this step.
Add garlic, ginger, and all spices. Stir 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add tinned tomatoes. Simmer 10 minutes until sauce darkens slightly.
Add chickpeas. Simmer 15 minutes until sauce thickens.
Add spinach in handfuls, stirring each in until wilted.
Season generously. Add a splash of water if too thick.
Serve over brown basmati rice. Top with yoghurt and fresh coriander.

recipes.title: Mushroom And Lentil Shepherd'S Pie
recipes.description: This plant-based adaptation of a British classic replaces lamb mince with lentils and mushrooms — providing equivalent protein (18g per serving) with substantially more fibre (12g…
recipes.clinical_notes: This plant-based adaptation of a British classic replaces lamb mince with lentils and mushrooms — providing equivalent protein (18g per serving) with substantially more fibre (12g vs 2g) and without the saturated fat associated with processed red meat, which WCRF UK classifies as a 'probable cause' of cancer. Porcini mushrooms add umami depth while providing ergothioneine — a unique antioxidant amino acid that accumulates selectively in cancer-vulnerable tissues including breast tissue. The sweet potato mash topping provides beta-carotene and potassium to counteract the sodium retention caused by corticosteroid anti-emetics used during chemotherapy.

recipes.title: Mediterranean Vegetable Tray Bake With Feta
recipes.description: A Mediterranean dietary pattern — characterised by abundant vegetables, olive oil, and minimal processed foods — is associated with a 16% reduction in breast cancer risk in the PRE…
recipes.clinical_notes: A Mediterranean dietary pattern — characterised by abundant vegetables, olive oil, and minimal processed foods — is associated with a 16% reduction in breast cancer risk in the PREDIMED-Plus randomised trial. This tray bake embodies Mediterranean eating: courgettes provide hydroxycinnamic acids; aubergine provides nasunin (a powerful anthocyanin that specifically protects brain cell membranes from lipid peroxidation — relevant to chemotherapy-induced cognitive effects); feta provides calcium. The high-oleic olive oil used for roasting provides oleocanthal — an anti-inflammatory compound with the same biological activity as ibuprofen at dietary doses.

recipes.title: Cauliflower And Chickpea Tikka Masala
recipes.description: Tikka masala is one of Britain's most popular dishes and this cancer-supportive plant-based version maintains all the flavour of the restaurant classic.
recipes.clinical_notes: Tikka masala is one of Britain's most popular dishes and this cancer-supportive plant-based version maintains all the flavour of the restaurant classic. Cauliflower's sulforaphane content (from glucoraphanin), combined with the curcumin in the curry spice base, provides complementary Nrf2 pathway activation and NF- κ B inhibition — two molecular targets that together comprehensively reduce pro-tumorigenic signalling. The tomato-based sauce creates a lycopene-rich matrix that is further enhanced by cooking with fat (coconut cream). Cancer Research UK identifies that maintaining enjoyment of familiar food is important for treatment adherence and quality of life.

recipes.title: Mixed Bean And Vegetable Chilli
recipes.description: A three-bean chilli (kidney, black, pinto) provides complementary amino acid profiles that together supply all essential amino acids in adequate quantities, meeting the protein req…
recipes.clinical_notes: A three-bean chilli (kidney, black, pinto) provides complementary amino acid profiles that together supply all essential amino acids in adequate quantities, meeting the protein requirements of cancer patients (1.2–2.0g/kg/day per ESPEN guidelines). The kidney beans' lectins, when properly cooked, have been shown to stimulate intestinal cell renewal — repairing the mucositis damage to gut lining caused by 5-fluorouracil and capecitabine chemotherapy. Chilli peppers' capsaicin at culinary doses induces TRPV1 receptor signalling in gut tissues that promotes serotonin release — improving gut motility without the adverse effects of serotonin drugs. Soluble fibre in beans (10g/cup) reduces LDL cholesterol in patients on AI therapy.

recipes.title: Wild Mushroom Risotto
recipes.description: Wild mushrooms (porcini, shiitake, oyster, chanterelle) each contain unique immunomodulatory polysaccharides at culinary concentrations.
recipes.clinical_notes: Wild mushrooms (porcini, shiitake, oyster, chanterelle) each contain unique immunomodulatory polysaccharides at culinary concentrations. Porcini provides ergosterol (provitamin D2 that converts to vitamin D when mushrooms are sun-dried), addressing the vitamin D deficiency prevalent in UK breast cancer patients (estimated 70% below optimal levels). Adequate vitamin D (≥30ng/ml serum 25-OHD) is associated with 40% better survival outcomes in breast cancer patients. Risotto's creamy starchy texture is particularly suitable for patients with mouth soreness or difficulty swallowing. Parmesan provides calcium and the umami-boosting glutamate that can overcome the taste alterations caused by zinc depletion during chemotherapy.

recipes.title: Coronation Chickpea Salad (Uk Classic Reinvented)
recipes.description: Coronation chicken — created for Queen Elizabeth II's 1953 coronation — is updated here with chickpeas.
recipes.clinical_notes: Coronation chicken — created for Queen Elizabeth II's 1953 coronation — is updated here with chickpeas. The coronation spice blend (curry powder, mango chutney, turmeric) provides curcumin alongside the unique anthocyanin profile of dried mango. Chickpeas replace chicken, providing equal protein with the additional benefits of plant-based saponins that prevent cholesterol absorption and reduce circulating oestrone sulfate. The mango and raisins provide quercetin and ellagic acid. This culturally familiar British dish maintains psychological connection to pre-cancer food enjoyment — an important aspect of quality of life during treatment recognised in MacMillan's Living Well Beyond Cancer programme.

recipes.title: Grilled Salmon With Lemon And Dill
recipes.description: Farmed and wild Atlantic salmon provides the highest EPA+DHA omega-3 content of commonly eaten UK fish (2.5–3.0g per 150g portion).
recipes.clinical_notes: Farmed and wild Atlantic salmon provides the highest EPA+DHA omega-3 content of commonly eaten UK fish (2.5–3.0g per 150g portion). These marine omega-3 fatty acids inhibit breast cancer cell invasion and metastasis through multiple mechanisms: suppression of MMP-2 and MMP-9 enzymes that degrade extracellular matrix; reduction of arachidonic acid-derived PGE2 that promotes angiogenesis; and direct incorporation into cell membranes that alters receptor signalling. The WCRF UK Second Expert Report recommends oily fish twice weekly for cancer survivors. Dill provides flavonoids including quercetin and isorhamnetin that have demonstrated pro-apoptotic activity against ER+ breast cancer cells in UK laboratory studies.

recipes.title: Mackerel With Beetroot And Horseradish
recipes.description: Mackerel is the UK's most omega-3-rich oily fish (4.5g EPA+DHA per 150g), substantially exceeding salmon.
recipes.clinical_notes: Mackerel is the UK's most omega-3-rich oily fish (4.5g EPA+DHA per 150g), substantially exceeding salmon. As a cold-water UK coastal species, mackerel is also highly sustainable and affordable — accessible to patients across all socioeconomic groups. Beetroot provides betalains that support liver detoxification pathways; horseradish contains sinigrin glucosinolate that is hydrolysed to allyl isothiocyanate — one of the most potent anti-cancer isothiocyanates. The fibre and polyphenols in beetroot complement the omega-3s to provide comprehensive anti-inflammatory coverage.

recipes.title: Chicken And Vegetable Casserole
recipes.description: British chicken casserole represents the gold standard of cancer-supportive comfort food.
recipes.clinical_notes: British chicken casserole represents the gold standard of cancer-supportive comfort food. Skinless chicken breast provides 31g lean protein per 100g — the highest biological value protein available that directly supports muscle protein synthesis at the rate needed to prevent cachexia. The gelatin released from bones during long cooking provides glycine and proline that repair the intestinal epithelium damaged by chemotherapy. Root vegetables (carrot, parsnip, swede) provide a rainbow of carotenoids. NHS oncology dietetics services across the UK rank chicken casserole as the most frequently recommended protein-rich comfort meal for patients on intensive chemotherapy.

recipes.title: Breast Cancer Prevention Power Smoothie
recipes.description: This smoothie combines the evidence-based breast cancer-preventive foods into one preparation: flaxseeds (lignans), blueberries (pterostilbene), spinach (folate), walnuts (ellagic…
recipes.clinical_notes: This smoothie combines the evidence-based breast cancer-preventive foods into one preparation: flaxseeds (lignans), blueberries (pterostilbene), spinach (folate), walnuts (ellagic acid), and fortified soy milk (isoflavones + calcium). Each ingredient addresses a distinct molecular pathway in breast cancer progression. The combination strategy is endorsed by the WCRF UK's '10 Cancer Prevention Recommendations' which include maintaining healthy weight, consuming wholegrains, limiting alcohol, and eating plant-rich foods — all embodied in this smoothie. Clinical oncology dietitians recommend this as a daily foundational drink for patients at all stages.

recipes.title: Baked Cinnamon Apple With Greek Yoghurt
recipes.description: Baked apples provide quercetin and pectin that together demonstrate synergistic anti-tumour activity.
recipes.clinical_notes: Baked apples provide quercetin and pectin that together demonstrate synergistic anti-tumour activity. The gentle cooking of apples increases the bioavailability of ursolic acid — a pentacyclic triterpenoid that inhibits STAT3 signalling (a transcription factor active in 40% of breast cancers). Greek yoghurt adds protein and probiotics, addressing the dual needs of muscle maintenance and gut microbiome health. Cinnamon provides cinnamaldehyde that has demonstrated selective toxicity to breast cancer cell lines while leaving normal cells unaffected. This simple dessert requires minimal preparation — valuable for patients experiencing fatigue, and provides warm comfort particularly during winter treatment cycles.

recipes.title: Dark Chocolate And Raspberry Mousse
recipes.description: Dark chocolate (>70% cocoa) provides a unique constellation of cancer-relevant compounds: flavanols (epicatechin, catechin) that activate Nrf2 antioxidant pathways; theobromine tha…
recipes.clinical_notes: Dark chocolate (>70% cocoa) provides a unique constellation of cancer-relevant compounds: flavanols (epicatechin, catechin) that activate Nrf2 antioxidant pathways; theobromine that promotes arterial vasodilation supporting tumour drug delivery; and magnesium (65mg/30g) that is essential for over 300 enzymatic reactions including DNA repair. Raspberries add ellagic acid and raspberry ketones that have demonstrated pro-apoptotic activity. Most importantly, this indulgent dessert supports the psychological wellbeing of cancer patients — the pleasure of food enjoyment is recognised by Macmillan Cancer Support as an essential quality-of-life component that can be safely maintained through evidence-based nutritional choices.
